requirements.condition: When a client and server communicate using QUIC

requirements.required_behavior: Encrypt as much of the packet as is practical.

requirements.condition: When creating a QUIC stream

requirements.required_behavior: Allow both endpoints to send data on the stream.

requirements.condition: When a stream is unidirectional

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow both endpoints to send data on the stream.

evidence.quote: unidirectional streams, which allow a single endpoint to send data.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Permit stream creation or data transmission beyond the available credit.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can exhaust advertised credit and verify that additional streams or data are not permitted until more credit is available.

requirements.condition: When transmitting QUIC traffic

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Transmit without congestion control.

requirements.condition: When implementing a QUIC stream.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept x with a length below A or above B.

requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's stream types and permitted send directions can be inspected or exercised for both stated alternatives.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint should not retransmit the lost stream data instead of sending RESET_STREAM.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-recovery test can declare outstanding data lost and distinguish RESET_STREAM transmission from data retransmission.

requirements.condition: When an implementation sends or receives stream data on a QUIC connection.

requirements.why_checkable: Implementation behavior can be tested to confirm that both per-stream and connection-wide flow-control limits constrain stream data.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not permit the sender to exceed either the applicable per-stream maximum or the aggregate maximum across all streams.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary per-stream and aggregate transmitted data and verify that the receiver maintains and enforces both maxima over the connection state.

evidence.quote: A QUIC receiver controls the maximum amount of data the sender can send on a stream as well as across all streams at any time

evidence.quote: a QUIC endpoint controls the maximum cumulative number of streams that its peer can initiate

requirements.condition: After initial limits have been established and the receiver advertises a larger stream limit
requirements.required_behavior: Use a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame to advertise the larger stream limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can verify that post-handshake stream-limit increases are conveyed using MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

evidence.quote: Subsequently, a receiver sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames (Section 19.10) or MAX_DATA frames (Section 19.9) to the sender to advertise larger limits.

requirements.condition: After initial limits have been established and the receiver advertises a larger connection limit
requirements.required_behavior: Use a MAX_DATA frame to advertise the larger connection limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can verify that post-handshake connection-limit increases are conveyed using MAX_DATA frames.

evidence.quote: Subsequently, a receiver sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames (Section 19.10) or MAX_DATA frames (Section 19.9) to the sender to advertise larger limits.

requirements.condition: When advertising a larger limit for a particular stream
requirements.required_behavior: Send a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame containing the corresponding stream ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream associated with a limit increase can be compared with the stream ID encoded in the frame.

evidence.quote: A receiver can advertise a larger limit for a stream by sending a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame with the corresponding stream ID.

requirements.condition: When interpreting or generating a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Interpret the value as a relative increment or as a non-offset byte count.

evidence.quote: A MAX_STREAM_DATA frame indicates the maximum absolute byte offset of a stream.

requirements.condition: When interpreting or generating a MAX_DATA frame

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Interpret its value as a per-stream limit or as a relative increment.
requirements.why_checkable: The MAX_DATA value can be compared with the sum of absolute offsets maintained across streams.

evidence.quote: A receiver can advertise a larger limit for a connection by sending a MAX_DATA frame, which indicates the maximum of the sum of the absolute byte offsets of all streams.

requirements.condition: As stream data is received
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain cumulative received-data accounting across streams and use flow-control accounting to check advertised connection and stream limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Internal accounting or focused traces can verify that received data updates limit checks across streams.

evidence.quote: A receiver maintains a cumulative sum of bytes received on all streams, which is used to check for violations of the advertised connection or stream data limits.

requirements.condition: When a receiver advertises a connection or stream limit smaller than one it previously advertised
requirements.error_behavior: Do not treat the smaller-limit advertisement as an error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a decreased limit and observe whether the endpoint raises an error.

evidence.quote: Once a receiver advertises a limit for the connection or a stream, it is not an error to advertise a smaller limit, but the smaller limit has no effect.

requirements.condition: When a receiver advertises a connection or stream limit smaller than one it previously advertised
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the previously effective higher limit unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reduce the effective flow-control limit to the newly advertised smaller value.
requirements.why_checkable: The effective limit before and after a decreased advertisement can be compared.

evidence.quote: Once a receiver advertises a limit for the connection or a stream, it is not an error to advertise a smaller limit, but the smaller limit has no effect.

requirements.condition: If the sender violates an advertised stream data limit

requirements.error_behavior: Use an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can send data beyond a stream limit and verify both connection closure and the reported error type.

requirements.condition: If the sender violates an advertised connection data limit
requirements.required_behavior: Close the connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Use an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can send data beyond the connection limit and verify both connection closure and the reported error type.

evidence.quote: A receiver MUST close the connection with an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if the sender violates the advertised connection or stream data limits; see Section 11 for details on error handling.

requirements.condition: When a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame does not increase the applicable stream flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the frame and preserve the existing effective stream limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply a non-increasing MAX_STREAM_DATA value as a new effective limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A non-increasing MAX_STREAM_DATA frame can be injected and the effective stream limit observed.

evidence.quote: A sender MUST ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frames that do not increase flow control limits.

requirements.condition: When a MAX_DATA frame does not increase the connection flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the frame and preserve the existing effective connection limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply a non-increasing MAX_DATA value as a new effective limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A non-increasing MAX_DATA frame can be injected and the effective connection limit observed.

evidence.quote: A sender MUST ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frames that do not increase flow control limits.

requirements.condition: When a sender has sent data up to the applicable flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the sender as flow-control blocked and refrain from sending new data governed by that limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send new data beyond the exhausted limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Sender state and emitted data can be observed after its sent offset reaches the active limit.

evidence.quote: If a sender has sent data up to the limit, it will be unable to send new data and is considered blocked.

requirements.condition: When the sender has data to write but is blocked by the connection flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Send a DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate the blocked condition to the receiver.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust the connection limit while retaining queued data and observe whether DATA_BLOCKED is sent.

evidence.quote: A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate to the receiver that it has data to write but is blocked by flow control limits.

requirements.condition: When the sender has data to write but is blocked by a stream flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate the blocked condition to the receiver.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust a stream limit while retaining queued data and observe whether STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED is sent.

evidence.quote: A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate to the receiver that it has data to write but is blocked by flow control limits.

requirements.condition: When the sender is limited by stream flow control and has no ack-eliciting packets in flight
requirements.required_behavior: Periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed test can maintain stream-level blocking with no ack-eliciting packets in flight and observe periodic frame emission.

evidence.quote: To keep the connection from closing, a sender that is flow control limited SHOULD periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame when it has no ack-eliciting packets in flight.

requirements.condition: When the sender is limited by connection flow control and has no ack-eliciting packets in flight
requirements.required_behavior: Periodically send a DATA_BLOCKED frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed test can maintain connection-level blocking with no ack-eliciting packets in flight and observe periodic frame emission.

evidence.quote: To keep the connection from closing, a sender that is flow control limited SHOULD periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame when it has no ack-eliciting packets in flight.

requirements.condition: When a receiver seeks to avoid blocking a sender.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation permits the receiver to send MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA multiple times within one round trip, or sufficiently early to allow for loss and recovery.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can observe whether the receiver supports either permitted transmission strategy without rejecting or suppressing repeated or early flow-control frames.

evidence.quote: To avoid blocking a sender, a receiver MAY send a MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frame multiple times within a round trip or send it early enough to allow time for loss of the frame and subsequent recovery.

requirements.condition: When a receiver is to advertise additional connection-level credit using MAX_DATA.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver sends MAX_DATA according to its credit-advertisement policy without requiring prior receipt of DATA_BLOCKED.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The receiver must not condition sending MAX_DATA on first receiving DATA_BLOCKED.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust connection-level credit while withholding DATA_BLOCKED and verify that the receiver's MAX_DATA transmission is not gated on that frame.

evidence.quote: Therefore, a receiver MUST NOT wait for a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame before sending a MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frame;

requirements.condition: When a receiver is to advertise additional stream-level credit using MAX_STREAM_DATA.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver sends MAX_STREAM_DATA according to its credit-advertisement policy without requiring prior receipt of STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The receiver must not condition sending MAX_STREAM_DATA on first receiving STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust stream-level credit while withholding STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED and verify that the receiver's MAX_STREAM_DATA transmission is not gated on that frame.

evidence.quote: Therefore, a receiver MUST NOT wait for a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame before sending a MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frame;

requirements.condition: For every stream whose bytes contribute to connection-level flow control accounting.
requirements.required_behavior: Endpoints eventually agree on the amount of flow-control credit consumed on the stream and account for all bytes at the connection level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Endpoints must not leave per-stream consumed credit permanently inconsistent or omit stream bytes from connection-level flow-control accounting.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can compare the peers' eventual consumed-credit accounting for each stream and verify that all stream bytes are included in connection-level accounting.

evidence.quote: Endpoints need to eventually agree on the amount of flow control credit that has been consumed on every stream, to be able to account for all bytes for connection-level flow control.

requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a RESET_STREAM frame for a matching stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint tears down state for the matching stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not retain the stream's operational state after processing the reset.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream state can be inspected after RESET_STREAM processing to verify that the matching stream was torn down.

evidence.quote: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint will tear down state for the matching stream and ignore further data arriving on that stream.

requirements.condition: Data arrives on a stream after the endpoint has received a RESET_STREAM frame for that stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint ignores the further arriving data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not deliver or otherwise process further arriving data as stream data.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can inject stream data after RESET_STREAM and verify that it is neither delivered nor processed.

evidence.quote: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint will tear down state for the matching stream and ignore further data arriving on that stream.

requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM frame is applied to a stream direction.
requirements.required_behavior: The affected direction enters an abruptly terminated state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The RESET_STREAM must not terminate more than the affected stream direction.
requirements.why_checkable: The state transition of the affected stream direction can be observed after processing RESET_STREAM.

evidence.quote: RESET_STREAM terminates one direction of a stream abruptly.

requirements.condition: RESET_STREAM terminates one direction of a bidirectional stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Data flow in the opposite direction remains unaffected.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not stop, reset, or otherwise alter opposite-direction data flow solely because RESET_STREAM was applied to the other direction.
requirements.why_checkable: A bidirectional-stream test can reset one direction and verify that data continues to flow normally in the opposite direction.

evidence.quote: For a bidirectional stream, RESET_STREAM has no effect on data flow in the opposite direction.

requirements.condition: One direction of a bidirectional stream has been terminated by RESET_STREAM while the opposite direction has not entered a terminal state.
requirements.required_behavior: Both endpoints maintain flow-control state for the stream in the unterminated direction until that direction enters a terminal state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Neither endpoint may discard the unterminated direction's flow-control state before that direction enters a terminal state.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can reset one direction and inspect flow-control tracking throughout the opposite direction's lifetime, including its transition to a terminal state.

evidence.quote: Both endpoints MUST maintain flow control state for the stream in the unterminated direction until that direction enters a terminal state.

requirements.condition: When determining connection-level flow control credit consumed by a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the stream's final size as the amount of flow control credit consumed by that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's flow-control accounting can be checked against the stream's final-size value.

evidence.quote: The final size is the amount of flow control credit that is consumed by a stream.

requirements.condition: Every contiguous byte on the stream was sent exactly once.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the final size equal to the number of bytes sent.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send a contiguous, non-retransmitted byte sequence and compare its byte count with the computed final size.

evidence.quote: Assuming that every contiguous byte on the stream was sent once, the final size is the number of bytes sent.

requirements.condition: When determining a stream's final size in the general case.
requirements.required_behavior: Use one plus the largest byte offset sent, or zero when no bytes were sent.
requirements.why_checkable: Observed transmitted offsets and the no-data case determine an exact expected final-size value.

evidence.quote: More generally, this is one higher than the offset of the byte with the largest offset sent on the stream, or zero if no bytes were sent.

requirements.condition: A stream is terminated by any mechanism.
requirements.required_behavior: Reliably communicate the stream's final size to the receiver.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Terminating a stream without reliable communication of its final size.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can exercise each termination path and verify that the peer reliably receives a final-size indication.

evidence.quote: A sender always communicates the final size of a stream to the receiver reliably, no matter how the stream is terminated.

requirements.condition: A STREAM frame carrying the FIN flag communicates the final size.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the final size as Offset plus Length, including when either field is implicit.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame's explicit or inferred Offset and Length yield an exact expected final size.

evidence.quote: The final size is the sum of the Offset and Length fields of a STREAM frame with a FIN flag, noting that these fields might be implicit.

requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM frame terminates the stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the RESET_STREAM frame's Final Size field to carry the stream final size.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Final Size field can be compared directly with the stream's expected final size.

evidence.quote: Alternatively, the Final Size field of a RESET_STREAM frame carries this value.

requirements.condition: The receiving part of a stream enters the "Size Known" or "Reset Recvd" state.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the stream's final size as known.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-transition test can verify that final-size knowledge is established upon entry into either named state.

evidence.quote: An endpoint will know the final size for a stream when the receiving part of the stream enters the "Size Known" or "Reset Recvd" state (Section 3).

requirements.condition: The receiver accounts for bytes sent on a stream in connection-level flow control.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the stream's final size to account for all bytes sent on that stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a value other than the final size for the stream's total contribution to connection-level flow-control accounting.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-level flow-control counters can be inspected after stream completion and compared with the final size.

evidence.quote: The receiver MUST use the final size of the stream to account for all bytes sent on the stream in its connection-level flow controller.

requirements.condition: A stream has a final size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending any data whose offset is equal to or greater than the stream's final size.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated STREAM data offsets can be checked against the known final-size boundary.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT send data on a stream at or beyond the final size.

requirements.condition: A stream's final size has become known.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep that final size immutable for the remainder of the stream's retained state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Changing the known final size.
requirements.why_checkable: The stored final size can be compared before and after subsequent STREAM or RESET_STREAM frames.

evidence.quote: Once a final size for a stream is known, it cannot change.

requirements.condition: A received RESET_STREAM or STREAM frame indicates a final size different from the already known final size.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, subject to the SHOULD-level exception.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish a final size, inject either frame type with an inconsistent size, and observe the error response.

evidence.quote: If a RESET_STREAM or STREAM frame is received indicating a change in the final size for the stream, an endpoint SHOULD respond with an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR; see Section 11 for details on error handling.

requirements.condition: The receiver receives data at an offset equal to or greater than the final size, including after stream closure.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the receipt as an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, subject to the SHOULD-level exception.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver boundary-violating data before or after closure and observe whether FINAL_SIZE_ERROR is produced.

evidence.quote: A receiver SHOULD treat receipt of data at or beyond the final size as an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, even after a stream is closed.

requirements.condition: The endpoint does not retain final-size state needed to detect these violations, particularly for closed streams.
requirements.error_behavior: Generation of the described FINAL_SIZE_ERROR errors is not mandatory.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage explicitly permits implementations not to generate these errors, so absence of the error cannot by itself be classified as noncompliance.

evidence.quote: Generating these errors is not mandatory, because requiring that an endpoint generate these errors also means that the endpoint needs to maintain the final size state for closed streams, which could mean a significant state commitment.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint opens a stream under the applicable incoming-stream limit.
requirements.required_behavior: The stream ID must be less than (max_streams * 4 + first_stream_id_of_type).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Opening a stream whose stream ID is equal to or greater than (max_streams * 4 + first_stream_id_of_type).
requirements.why_checkable: A test can set max_streams and the first stream ID for the type, then verify acceptance below the computed bound and rejection at or above it.

evidence.quote: Only streams with a stream ID less than "(max_streams * 4 + first_stream_id_of_type)" can be opened; see Table 1.

requirements.condition: When establishing the initial stream limits.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the initial stream limits using transport parameters.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake transport parameters and the resulting initial stream limits can be inspected and compared.

evidence.quote: Initial limits are set in the transport parameters; see Section 18.2.

requirements.condition: When advertising a stream limit after the initial limits have been set.
requirements.required_behavior: Advertise the subsequent limit using a MAX_STREAMS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect whether post-initial stream-limit advertisements use MAX_STREAMS frames.

evidence.quote: Subsequent limits are advertised using MAX_STREAMS frames; see Section 19.11.

requirements.condition: When tracking or enforcing stream concurrency limits.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using one shared concurrency limit for both unidirectional and bidirectional streams.

evidence.quote: Separate limits apply to unidirectional and bidirectional streams.

requirements.condition: When a max_streams transport parameter is received with a value greater than 2^60.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Keeping the connection open or delaying closure after receiving the offending transport parameter.
requirements.error_behavior: Immediately close the connection with a TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a max_streams transport parameter above 2^60 and observe the timing and error type of connection closure.

evidence.quote: If either is received, the connection MUST be closed immediately with a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR if the offending value was received in a transport parameter

requirements.condition: When a MAX_STREAMS frame is received with a value greater than 2^60.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Keeping the connection open or delaying closure after receiving the offending frame.
requirements.error_behavior: Immediately close the connection with a FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a MAX_STREAMS frame carrying a value above 2^60 and observe the timing and error type of connection closure.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint opens streams subject to a limit set by its peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Opening streams beyond the peer's applicable stream limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can advertise a known limit and count whether the endpoint opens more streams than permitted.

evidence.quote: Endpoints MUST NOT exceed the limit set by their peer.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a frame containing a stream ID that exceeds the stream limit the endpoint advertised.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting or processing the limit-exceeding stream ID without treating it as the specified connection error.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the violation as a connection error of type STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can advertise a limit, deliver a frame with a stream ID beyond that limit, and inspect the resulting connection error.

evidence.quote: An endpoint that receives a frame with a stream ID exceeding the limit it has sent MUST treat this as a connection error of type STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR

requirements.condition: When a receiver has advertised a stream limit using MAX_STREAMS and later advertises a smaller limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the previously effective, larger stream limit unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reducing the effective stream limit to the subsequently advertised smaller value.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can process decreasing MAX_STREAMS values and verify that the effective limit never decreases.

evidence.quote: Once a receiver advertises a stream limit using the MAX_STREAMS frame, advertising a smaller limit has no effect.

requirements.condition: When a MAX_STREAMS frame carries a value less than or equal to the current stream limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the MAX_STREAMS frame and leave the effective stream limit unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Changing stream-limit state or credit in response to a non-increasing MAX_STREAMS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can deliver equal and smaller MAX_STREAMS values and verify that neither changes the current limit.

evidence.quote: MAX_STREAMS frames that do not increase the stream limit MUST be ignored.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint cannot open a new stream because of the peer's stream limits.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust the peer-provided stream credit, attempt another stream opening, and observe whether STREAMS_BLOCKED is sent.

evidence.quote: An endpoint that is unable to open a new stream due to the peer's limits SHOULD send a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame (Section 19.14).

requirements.condition: When an endpoint can advertise additional stream credit and has not received a STREAMS_BLOCKED signal.
requirements.required_behavior: Advertise additional credit according to its own policy without making receipt of STREAMS_BLOCKED a prerequisite.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Waiting for a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame before advertising additional stream credit.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can withhold STREAMS_BLOCKED and verify that additional credit advertisement is not gated on receiving that frame.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT wait to receive this signal before advertising additional credit

requirements.condition: During the handshake phase
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoints negotiate the application protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated application protocol can be inspected after or during a handshake.

evidence.quote: and negotiate the application protocol.

requirements.required_behavior: The handshake confirms that both endpoints are willing to communicate.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can be tested to ensure handshake confirmation is reached only after mutual willingness to communicate has been established.

evidence.quote: The handshake (Section 7) confirms that both endpoints are willing to communicate (Section 8.1)

requirements.condition: During the handshake
requirements.required_behavior: The handshake establishes parameters for the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection state after the handshake can be inspected for established connection parameters.

evidence.quote: and establishes parameters for the connection (Section 7.4).

requirements.condition: During the handshake phase
requirements.required_behavior: Application-protocol use of the connection is permitted subject to unspecified limitations.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage does not identify the limitations, so complete conformant behavior cannot be determined from this chunk.

requirements.required_behavior: The client is permitted to send application data.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime trace can verify that client application data is accepted for transmission before any server response is received.

evidence.quote: 0-RTT allows application data to be sent by a client before receiving a response from the server.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not treat 0-RTT as providing replay protection.

requirements.why_checkable: Path-change tests can verify that a connection identified by connection IDs continues on a new path for both endpoint-selected and externally forced changes.

requirements.condition: When a connection is no longer needed or desired
requirements.required_behavior: A client or server can terminate the connection using one of several unspecified mechanisms.
requirements.why_checkable: The mechanisms and their required behavior are only referenced and are not present in this chunk, so the constraint cannot be fully validated from the supplied evidence.

evidence.quote: For connections that are no longer needed or desired, there are several ways for a client and server to terminate a connection, as described in Section 10.

requirements.condition: When establishing a new connection from a long-header packet
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Source Connection ID and Destination Connection ID fields to set the connection IDs for the new connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-establishment tests can compare the resulting connection-ID state with the two fields in the initiating long-header packet.

evidence.quote: These fields are used to set the connection IDs for new connections; see Section 7.2 for details.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a packet with a short header
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Destination Connection ID without an explicit connection-ID length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A short header must not include a Source Connection ID or an explicit Destination Connection ID length.
requirements.why_checkable: The short-header wire layout can be inspected for the Destination Connection ID and absence of the excluded fields.

evidence.quote: Packets with short headers (Section 17.3) only include the Destination Connection ID and omit the explicit length.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint encodes or parses the Destination Connection ID in a short header
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint must know the Destination Connection ID length from context because the short header does not encode it explicitly.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can verify that the endpoint determines the field boundary without reading an explicit length from the short header.

evidence.quote: The length of the Destination Connection ID field is expected to be known to endpoints.

requirements.condition: When generating a Version Negotiation packet in response to a client packet
requirements.required_behavior: Echo the connection IDs selected by the client.
requirements.why_checkable: A generated Version Negotiation packet can be compared with the connection IDs in the triggering client packet.

evidence.quote: A Version Negotiation (Section 17.2.1) packet echoes the connection IDs selected by the client

requirements.condition: When multiple concurrent connections use zero-length connection IDs and peer connection migration, NAT rebinding, or client port reuse might be in use
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not use the same local IP address and port for those concurrent connections.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime connection state can be checked for concurrent zero-length-ID connections sharing a local address and port under the listed protocol features.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT use the same IP address and port for multiple concurrent connections with zero-length connection IDs, unless it is certain that those protocol features are not in use.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint uses a non-zero-length connection ID
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the peer has a supply of connection IDs available for packets sent to the endpoint.
requirements.why_checkable: Protocol traces and endpoint state can verify that usable peer-held connection IDs remain available.

evidence.quote: When an endpoint uses a non-zero-length connection ID, it needs to ensure that the peer has a supply of connection IDs from which to choose for packets sent to the endpoint.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint supplies the peer with connection IDs for packets sent to that endpoint
requirements.required_behavior: Supply those connection IDs using NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame traces can be inspected to confirm that supplied connection IDs are carried in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.

evidence.quote: These connection IDs are supplied by the endpoint using the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame (Section 19.15).

requirements.condition: For each connection ID managed by the endpoint.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the connection ID with a sequence number used to correlate references in NEW_CONNECTION_ID and RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-ID state and frame processing can be inspected to verify that each applicable connection ID has an associated sequence number.

evidence.quote: Each connection ID has an associated sequence number to assist in detecting when NEW_CONNECTION_ID or RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames refer to the same value.

requirements.condition: For the initial connection ID issued by an endpoint in the Source Connection ID field during the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign sequence number 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign any sequence number other than 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial connection ID's recorded sequence number can be compared with the fixed value 0.

evidence.quote: The sequence number of the initial connection ID is 0.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends the preferred_address transport parameter containing a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign sequence number 1 to the supplied connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign the supplied connection ID any sequence number other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport parameter and the associated connection-ID sequence number are directly observable.

evidence.quote: If the preferred_address transport parameter is sent, the sequence number of the supplied connection ID is 1.

requirements.condition: When communicating additional connection IDs to the peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Communicate them using NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frames can be inspected to determine how additional connection IDs are communicated.

evidence.quote: Additional connection IDs are communicated to the peer using NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames (Section 19.15).

requirements.condition: Whenever an endpoint newly issues a sequenced connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Set its sequence number to exactly one greater than the preceding newly issued connection ID's sequence number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse, decrease, skip, or otherwise increment the sequence number by a value other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of issued connection IDs can be checked for exact unit increments.

evidence.quote: The sequence number on each newly issued connection ID MUST increase by 1.

requirements.condition: For the connection ID selected by a client for its first Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the connection ID without an assigned sequence number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a sequence number to that connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The client's first Destination Connection ID and its metadata can be inspected directly.

evidence.quote: The connection ID that a client selects for the first Destination Connection ID field it sends and any connection ID provided by a Retry packet are not assigned sequence numbers.

requirements.condition: For any connection ID provided by a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the connection ID without an assigned sequence number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a sequence number to that connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: A Retry-provided connection ID and its metadata can be inspected directly.

evidence.quote: The connection ID that a client selects for the first Destination Connection ID field it sends and any connection ID provided by a Retry packet are not assigned sequence numbers.

requirements.condition: After an endpoint issues a connection ID and before the connection ends or the peer retires that connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept packets carrying the issued connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject packets merely because they carry that issued, non-retired connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet acceptance can be tested before and after receipt of the corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.

evidence.quote: When an endpoint issues a connection ID, it MUST accept packets that carry this connection ID for the duration of the connection or until its peer invalidates the connection ID via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame (Section 19.16).

requirements.condition: When a connection ID has been issued and has not been retired.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the connection ID as active.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat the connection ID as inactive solely while it remains issued and unretired.
requirements.why_checkable: The active set can be compared with issuance and retirement state.

evidence.quote: Connection IDs that are issued and not retired are considered active;

requirements.condition: For an active connection ID on the current connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit its use at any time and in any packet type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Restrict its validity to particular times or packet types solely on that basis.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet processing can be exercised across packet types and connection phases with an active connection ID.

evidence.quote: any active connection ID is valid for use with the current connection at any time, in any packet type.

requirements.condition: When the server issued a connection ID through the preferred_address transport parameter and that ID is active.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat that connection ID as valid for the current connection at any time and in any packet type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exclude it from the validity rules applied to other active connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The origin of the connection ID and subsequent packet acceptance are observable.

evidence.quote: This includes the connection ID issued by the server via the preferred_address transport parameter.

requirements.condition: While maintaining connection IDs for a peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the peer has a sufficient number of available, unused connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's available unused connection-ID pool can be observed, but the chunk does not define a measurable threshold for “sufficient.”

evidence.quote: An endpoint SHOULD ensure that its peer has a sufficient number of available and unused connection IDs.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint advertises how many active connection IDs it is willing to maintain.
requirements.required_behavior: Express that number using the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport parameters can be inspected for the advertised limit.

evidence.quote: Endpoints advertise the number of active connection IDs they are willing to maintain using the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.

requirements.condition: When providing connection IDs to a peer that has advertised a limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the number of provided connection IDs within the peer's limit, except for the expressly permitted temporary-excess case.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Provide more connection IDs than the peer's limit without simultaneously causing sufficient retirement of excess IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The peer's advertised limit and the number and retirement effects of provided IDs can be counted.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT provide more connection IDs than the peer's limit.

requirements.condition: When sending connection IDs would temporarily exceed the peer's active-connection-ID limit.
requirements.required_behavior: In the same NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame, set Retire Prior To high enough to require retirement of every excess connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Temporarily exceed the peer's limit without the same frame requiring retirement of all excess IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting count and the Retire Prior To value in the frame can be evaluated together.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MAY send connection IDs that temporarily exceed a peer's limit if the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame also requires the retirement of any excess, by including a sufficiently large value in the Retire Prior To field.

requirements.condition: After processing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame, including all additions and retirements, when the active connection-ID count exceeds the endpoint's advertised active_connection_id_limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Keep the connection open after detecting the post-processing limit violation.
requirements.error_behavior: Use an error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted frame can produce the excess count, after which connection closure and its error type are observable.

evidence.quote: After processing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame and adding and retiring active connection IDs, if the number of active connection IDs exceeds the value advertised in its active_connection_id_limit transport parameter, an endpoint MUST close the connection with an error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

requirements.condition: When the peer retires a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Supply a new connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Receipt of retirement and subsequent issuance of a replacement connection ID can be observed.

evidence.quote: An endpoint SHOULD supply a new connection ID when the peer retires a connection ID.

requirements.condition: When the endpoint has provided fewer connection IDs than the peer's active_connection_id_limit and receives a packet using a previously unused connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to supply a new connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The issued-ID count, peer limit, received packet's connection ID, and any subsequent issuance are observable.

evidence.quote: If an endpoint provided fewer connection IDs than the peer's active_connection_id_limit, it MAY supply a new connection ID when it receives a packet with a previously unused connection ID.

requirements.condition: For each connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to impose a limit on the total number of connection IDs it issues.
requirements.why_checkable: Issuance behavior can be tested against the endpoint's configured or implemented per-connection cap.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MAY limit the total number of connection IDs issued for each connection to avoid the risk of running out of connection IDs;

requirements.condition: When controlling connection-ID issuance and associated per-path state.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to limit connection-ID issuance.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's issuance policy and resulting issued-ID count can be observed.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MAY also limit the issuance of connection IDs to reduce the amount of per-path state it maintains, such as path validation status, as its peer might interact with it over as many paths as there are issued connection IDs.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates migration and requires non-zero-length connection IDs.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the peer's available connection-ID pool contains a connection ID it can newly use for the migration.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Initiate such migration with no available new connection ID for the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: The peer's available pool at migration initiation can be checked for at least one usable new connection ID.

evidence.quote: An endpoint that initiates migration and requires non-zero-length connection IDs SHOULD ensure that the pool of connection IDs available to its peer allows the peer to use a new connection ID on migration, as the peer will be unable to respond if the pool is exhausted.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint selected a zero-length connection ID during the handshake.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Issue any new connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake selection and later connection-ID issuance are directly observable.

evidence.quote: An endpoint that selects a zero-length connection ID during the handshake cannot issue a new connection ID.

requirements.condition: For every packet sent toward an endpoint that selected a zero-length connection ID during the handshake, regardless of network path.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a zero-length Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a non-zero-length Destination Connection ID field.
requirements.why_checkable: Destination Connection ID field lengths can be inspected across all packets and paths directed to the endpoint.

evidence.quote: A zero-length Destination Connection ID field is used in all packets sent toward such an endpoint over any network path.

requirements.condition: While maintaining connection IDs supplied by a peer and sending packets to that peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain the peer-supplied connection IDs as a set of available connection IDs from which an ID can be selected for sending packets.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's connection-ID state and its packet-sending selection can be inspected to verify that received IDs are tracked and available for use.

evidence.quote: An endpoint maintains a set of connection IDs received from its peer, any of which it can use when sending packets.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint removes a connection ID from use.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for that connection ID to the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger local removal of a connection ID and observe whether the corresponding retirement frame is sent.

evidence.quote: When the endpoint wishes to remove a connection ID from use, it sends a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame to its peer.

requirements.condition: After an endpoint sends a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for a connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use that connection ID again.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets sent after the retirement frame can be inspected for reuse of the retired connection ID.

evidence.quote: Sending a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame indicates that the connection ID will not be used again

requirements.condition: When a peer processes a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Replace the retired connection ID by supplying a new connection ID in a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The described retirement request and replacement mechanism directly identify the expected observable response, although the passage does not state a strict deadline.

evidence.quote: Sending a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame indicates that the connection ID will not be used again and requests that the peer replace it with a new connection ID using a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends packets using a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate use of that connection ID with one local-address and destination-address pair.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the same connection ID for packets sent from multiple local addresses or to multiple destination addresses.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces can correlate each connection ID with the local and destination address pair on which it is used.

evidence.quote: endpoints limit the use of a connection ID to packets sent from a single local address to a single destination address.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint is no longer actively using either the local address or the destination address associated with a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Retire that connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can discontinue use of either associated address and verify that the endpoint initiates retirement of the connection ID.

evidence.quote: Endpoints SHOULD retire connection IDs when they are no longer actively using either the local or destination address for which the connection ID was used.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint needs its peer to retire previously issued connection IDs.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame whose Retire Prior To field is increased to indicate the connection IDs to retire.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted frame type and whether its Retire Prior To value increased are directly observable.

evidence.quote: Such an endpoint can cause its peer to retire connection IDs by sending a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with an increased Retire Prior To field.

requirements.condition: After requesting retirement of previously issued connection IDs and before the peer retires them.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue accepting those previously issued connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can continue sending on an indicated ID before retiring it, allowing acceptance behavior to be observed.

evidence.quote: The endpoint SHOULD continue to accept the previously issued connection IDs until they are retired by the peer.

requirements.condition: If the endpoint can no longer process connection IDs indicated for retirement.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to close the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can make indicated IDs unprocessable and observe whether the implementation uses the permitted connection-close response.

evidence.quote: If the endpoint can no longer process the indicated connection IDs, it MAY close the connection.

requirements.condition: Upon receiving a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with an increased Retire Prior To field.
requirements.required_behavior: Stop using the connection IDs corresponding to the increased Retire Prior To value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send further packets using those connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces after receipt of the increased value can detect any continued use of the corresponding IDs.

evidence.quote: Upon receipt of an increased Retire Prior To field, the peer MUST stop using the corresponding connection IDs

requirements.condition: Upon receiving a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with an increased Retire Prior To field.
requirements.required_behavior: Send RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames to retire the corresponding connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The required retirement frames and their referenced connection IDs are observable on the wire.

evidence.quote: Upon receipt of an increased Retire Prior To field, the peer MUST stop using the corresponding connection IDs and retire them with RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames

requirements.condition: Upon receiving an increased Retire Prior To value together with a newly provided connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Stop using and retire all corresponding connection IDs before adding the newly provided connection ID to the active set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Add the newly provided connection ID to the active set before the corresponding old IDs have been stopped and retired.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation or a focused test can observe retirement actions and active-set insertion to verify their required ordering.

evidence.quote: the peer MUST stop using the corresponding connection IDs and retire them with RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames before adding the newly provided connection ID to the set of active connection IDs.

requirements.condition: While RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames for locally retired connection IDs remain unacknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: Bound the number of such locally retired connection IDs retained in the unacknowledged-retirement state.
requirements.why_checkable: The count of locally retired IDs with unacknowledged retirement frames can be inspected under sustained retirement and acknowledgment loss.

evidence.quote: An endpoint SHOULD limit the number of connection IDs it has retired locally for which RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames have not yet been acknowledged.

requirements.condition: When provisioning capacity to send and track RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Support sending and tracking at least two times the negotiated active_connection_id_limit value in RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A stress test can compare the implementation's retirement-frame tracking capacity with twice the transport-parameter value.

evidence.quote: An endpoint SHOULD allow for sending and tracking a number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames of at least twice the value of the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint discards or forgets a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Retire the connection ID before forgetting it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Forget a connection ID that has not been retired.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-ID lifecycle state can be inspected to ensure every discarded ID first enters the retired state.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT forget a connection ID without retiring it

requirements.condition: When the number of connection IDs needing retirement exceeds the retirement handling limit described in the paragraph.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to treat the condition as a connection error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exceed the retirement handling limit and verify the type of any resulting connection error.

evidence.quote: it MAY choose to treat having connection IDs in need of retirement that exceed this limit as a connection error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

requirements.condition: After issuing a Retire Prior To value and before receiving retirement frames for every connection ID it indicates.
requirements.required_behavior: Wait until RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames have been received for all connection IDs indicated by the previous value before issuing another Retire Prior To update.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Issue a Retire Prior To update while any connection ID indicated by the previous Retire Prior To value has not yet been retired by a received RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can compare Retire Prior To updates with receipt of retirement frames for all IDs covered by the preceding value.

evidence.quote: Endpoints SHOULD NOT issue updates of the Retire Prior To field before receiving RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames that retire all connection IDs indicated by the previous Retire Prior To value.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the packet on receipt.
requirements.why_checkable: A receipt-path test can verify that connection classification occurs when the packet is received.

evidence.quote: Incoming packets are classified on receipt.

requirements.condition: When an incoming packet is classified.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify it as associated with an existing connection or, at a server, as potentially creating a new connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A client must not classify an incoming packet as potentially creating a new connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's classification outcome and the server-only new-connection branch can be observed for incoming packets.

evidence.quote: Packets can either be associated with an existing connection or -- for servers -- potentially create a new connection.

requirements.condition: The packet has a non-zero-length Destination Connection ID corresponding to an existing connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Process the packet in association with that existing connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet carrying a known nonempty Destination Connection ID can be injected and its selected connection observed.

evidence.quote: If the packet has a non-zero-length Destination Connection ID corresponding to an existing connection, QUIC processes that packet accordingly.

requirements.condition: When connection IDs are associated with connections.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit more than one connection ID to map to the same connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not enforce a one-connection-ID-per-connection invariant.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection lookup state can be inspected or exercised with multiple connection IDs assigned to one connection.

evidence.quote: Note that more than one connection ID can be associated with a connection; see Section 5.1.

requirements.condition: The Destination Connection ID is zero length and the packet's addressing information matches that used by the endpoint to identify a zero-length-ID connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Process the packet as part of the matching connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet with a zero-length Destination Connection ID and matching address tuple can be sent and the selected connection observed.

evidence.quote: If the Destination Connection ID is zero length and the addressing information in the packet matches the addressing information the endpoint uses to identify a connection with a zero-length connection ID, QUIC processes the packet as part of that connection.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint identifies a connection having a zero-length connection ID from addressing information.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may use destination IP and port alone, or both source and destination addresses, as its identification key.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's connection-key construction or lookup behavior can be tested for either permitted addressing scheme.

evidence.quote: An endpoint can use just destination IP and port or both source and destination addresses for identification

requirements.condition: A packet cannot be attributed to an existing connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may send a Stateless Reset for that packet.
requirements.why_checkable: An unattributable packet can be delivered and the endpoint can be observed for an optional Stateless Reset response.

evidence.quote: Endpoints can send a Stateless Reset (Section 10.3) for any packets that cannot be attributed to an existing connection.

requirements.condition: A packet is matched to an existing connection but is inconsistent with that connection's state.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process the inconsistent packet as valid connection input.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can construct state-inconsistent packets that still match a connection and verify that they produce no accepted processing effects.

evidence.quote: Packets that are matched to an existing connection are discarded if the packets are inconsistent with the state of that connection.

requirements.condition: A packet matched to an existing connection indicates a protocol version different from the connection's version.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or process the packet under the existing connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection-matching packet bearing a different protocol version can be injected and its disposition observed.

evidence.quote: packets are discarded if they indicate a different protocol version than that of the connection

requirements.condition: The expected keys are available, but removal of packet protection from a packet matched to the connection is unsuccessful.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process the packet contents as authenticated connection input.
requirements.why_checkable: With expected keys installed, a packet whose protection cannot be removed can be supplied and checked for discard without state effects.

evidence.quote: packets are discarded if they indicate a different protocol version than that of the connection or if the removal of packet protection is unsuccessful once the expected keys are available.

requirements.condition: A packet is invalid and lacks strong integrity protection, including an Initial, Retry, or Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may discard the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed packets of the identified weakly protected classes can be supplied and discard behavior observed.

evidence.quote: Invalid packets that lack strong integrity protection, such as Initial, Retry, or Version Negotiation, MAY be discarded.

requirements.condition: Before discovering an error, the endpoint processed the contents of an invalid packet lacking strong integrity protection.
requirements.required_behavior: Either generate a connection error or fully revert every change made while processing the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue without a connection error while retaining any change made during the invalid packet's processing.
requirements.error_behavior: Generating a connection error satisfies the required alternative to fully reverting all processing changes.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted invalid weakly protected packet can cause provisional state changes before a later error, after which tests can verify either a connection error or complete rollback.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST generate a connection error if processing the contents of these packets prior to discovering an error, or fully revert any changes made during that processing.

requirements.condition: A valid packet is sent to a client.
requirements.required_behavior: The packet includes a Destination Connection ID matching a value selected by the client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treating a packet whose Destination Connection ID does not match a client-selected value as valid.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet validation can inspect the Destination Connection ID and compare it with the values selected by the client.

evidence.quote: Valid packets sent to clients always include a Destination Connection ID that matches a value the client selects.

requirements.condition: A received packet does not match an existing connection by Destination Connection ID, or by local IP address and port when the Destination Connection ID is zero length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continuing to process or accept the unmatched packet.
requirements.error_behavior: Discard the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a packet that matches neither the applicable connection ID nor the zero-length-ID address-and-port tuple and verify that it is discarded.

evidence.quote: Packets that do not match an existing connection -- based on Destination Connection ID or, if this value is zero length, local IP address and port -- are discarded.

requirements.condition: A client receives packets for a connection encrypted with a key that it has not yet computed.
requirements.required_behavior: The client is permitted to drop the packets or buffer them while awaiting later packets that enable computation of the key.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver packets encrypted with a not-yet-computed key and verify that either dropping or buffering is supported as permitted behavior.

evidence.quote: Due to packet reordering or loss, a client might receive packets for a connection that are encrypted with a key it has not yet computed. The client MAY drop these packets, or it MAY buffer them in anticipation of later packets that allow it to compute the key.

requirements.condition: A client receives a packet using a version different from the version it initially selected.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting or continuing to process the packet.
requirements.error_behavior: Discard the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send a packet with a version different from the client's initially selected version and observe whether the packet is discarded.

evidence.quote: If a client receives a packet that uses a different version than it initially selected, it MUST discard that packet.

requirements.condition: A server receives a packet indicating an unsupported version, and the packet is large enough to initiate a new connection for any supported version.
requirements.required_behavior: The server should send a Version Negotiation packet as described in Section 6.1.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a sufficiently large packet carrying an unsupported version and observe whether the server emits the specified packet type.

evidence.quote:
If a server receives a packet that indicates an unsupported version
   and if the packet is large enough to initiate a new connection for
   any supported version, the server SHOULD send a Version Negotiation
   packet as described in Section 6.1.  A server MAY limit the number of
   packets to which it responds with a Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.condition: The server receives packets to which it could respond with Version Negotiation packets.
requirements.required_behavior: The server may impose a limit on the number of packets that receive Version Negotiation responses.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be inspected or tested for a response-count limiting policy.

evidence.quote:
packet as described in Section 6.1.  A server MAY limit the number of
   packets to which it responds with a Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.condition: A server receives a smaller packet that specifies an unsupported version.
requirements.required_behavior: The server must drop the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not process or respond to the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send an undersized packet specifying an unsupported version and verify that it is dropped without a response or further processing.

evidence.quote: Servers MUST drop smaller packets that specify unsupported versions.

requirements.condition: A server receives a sufficiently long datagram using a version that the server does not support.
requirements.required_behavior: The server should respond with a Version Negotiation packet.
