requirements.forbidden_behavior: Govern 0-RTT frames using any non-remembered transport-parameter values.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can make remembered and newly learned values differ and observe the values respected by emitted 0-RTT frames.

evidence.quote: When sending frames in 0-RTT packets, a client MUST only use remembered transport parameters

requirements.condition: When a client has learned updated values from the server's updated transport parameters or from frames received in 1-RTT packets and is sending 0-RTT packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use those updated values for frames sent in 0-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can deliver larger updated values through both sources and verify that subsequent 0-RTT output does not use them.

evidence.quote: it MUST NOT use updated values that it learns from the server's updated transport parameters or from frames received in 1-RTT packets.

requirements.condition: When updated transport-parameter values are learned from the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply those updated values only to 1-RTT packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply handshake-updated values to 0-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-space-specific behavior can be tested using distinct remembered and handshake-updated values.

evidence.quote: Updated values of transport parameters from the handshake apply only to 1-RTT packets.

requirements.condition: When handshake transport parameters or frames sent in 1-RTT packets increase flow-control limits while the client can still send 0-RTT packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue applying the remembered flow-control limits to every 0-RTT packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the increased flow-control limits for any 0-RTT packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can raise the limit after 0-RTT begins and verify that every later 0-RTT packet remains within the remembered limit.

evidence.quote: flow control limits from remembered transport parameters apply to all 0-RTT packets even if those values are increased by the handshake or by frames sent in 1-RTT packets.

requirements.condition: When a client uses updated transport parameters in 0-RTT.
requirements.error_behavior: The server is permitted to treat the behavior as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send 0-RTT that relies on an updated value and verify that closing the connection with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION is an allowed response.

evidence.quote: A server MAY treat the use of updated transport parameters in 0-RTT as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a transport parameter that it does not support.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint must ignore the unsupported transport parameter.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not apply or act on the unsupported transport parameter.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can be given an unsupported transport parameter and observed to verify that processing continues without applying that parameter.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST ignore transport parameters that it does not support.

requirements.condition: When a transport parameter used to negotiate an optional protocol feature is absent.
requirements.required_behavior: The optional protocol feature negotiated by that parameter must be disabled.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not enable the optional protocol feature in the parameter's absence.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can omit the relevant transport parameter and verify that the associated optional feature remains disabled.

evidence.quote: The absence of a transport parameter therefore disables any optional protocol feature that is negotiated using the parameter.

requirements.condition: When CRYPTO data is received out of order.
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain a buffer for the out-of-order CRYPTO data.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can be inspected or tested to determine whether out-of-order CRYPTO data is retained in a buffer for later processing.

evidence.quote: Implementations need to maintain a buffer of CRYPTO data received out of order.

requirements.condition: When data is received in out-of-order CRYPTO frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Support buffering at least 4096 bytes of that data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not impose a supported out-of-order CRYPTO buffering capacity below 4096 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver up to 4096 bytes in out-of-order CRYPTO frames and verify that the implementation can buffer them.

evidence.quote: Implementations MUST support buffering at least 4096 bytes of data received in out-of-order CRYPTO frames.

requirements.condition: During the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to buffer more than the mandatory minimum amount of out-of-order CRYPTO data.
requirements.why_checkable: The configured or observed handshake buffering limit can be checked to confirm that capacities above 4096 bytes are accepted as conforming behavior.

evidence.quote: Endpoints MAY choose to allow more data to be buffered during the handshake.

requirements.condition: During the life of a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to vary its CRYPTO buffer size over time.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime observation or code inspection can determine whether the CRYPTO buffer limit is allowed to change across connection states.

evidence.quote: An endpoint's buffer size does not need to remain constant during the life of the connection.

requirements.condition: The endpoint's CRYPTO buffer is exceeded during the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to expand the buffer temporarily to complete the handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake test that exceeds the current buffer limit can verify whether temporary expansion is supported and confined to handshake completion.

evidence.quote: If an endpoint's buffer is exceeded during the handshake, it can expand its buffer temporarily to complete the handshake.

requirements.condition: The endpoint's CRYPTO buffer is exceeded during the handshake and the endpoint does not expand it.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not keep the connection open after declining to expand the exceeded handshake CRYPTO buffer.
requirements.error_behavior: Use the CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code when closing the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can overflow the handshake CRYPTO buffer while preventing expansion and verify both connection closure and the emitted error code.

evidence.quote: If an endpoint does not expand its buffer, it MUST close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.

requirements.condition: After handshake completion, the endpoint cannot buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame and chooses the discard response.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the unbufferable CRYPTO frame and every CRYPTO frame received afterward.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not resume accepting later CRYPTO frames after selecting the discard response.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger the discard branch and then send later CRYPTO frames to verify that all such future frames are also discarded.

evidence.quote: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future

requirements.condition: The handshake has completed and the endpoint cannot buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Choose a permitted response: discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future, or close the connection.
requirements.error_behavior: If the endpoint chooses connection closure, use the CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.
requirements.why_checkable: A post-handshake buffer-exhaustion test can verify that the endpoint follows one of the two specified response branches and uses the required error code for the closure branch.

evidence.quote: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future, or it MAY close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.

requirements.condition: A received packet contains a CRYPTO frame that the endpoint discards.
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge the packet containing the discarded CRYPTO frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not withhold acknowledgment merely because the contained CRYPTO frame was discarded.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send a packet whose CRYPTO frame is discarded and verify that the packet is nevertheless acknowledged.

evidence.quote: Packets containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged because the packet has been received and processed by the transport even though the CRYPTO frame was discarded.

requirements.condition: After an endpoint receives packets from an address that has not yet been validated.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint must limit the amount of data it sends to that unvalidated address to no more than three times the amount of data received from that address.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not send more than three times the amount of data received from the unvalidated address.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can track bytes received from an unvalidated address and verify that bytes sent to it do not exceed the stated 3:1 anti-amplification limit.

evidence.quote: Therefore, after receiving packets from an address that is not yet validated, an endpoint MUST limit the amount of data it sends to the unvalidated address to three times the amount of data received from that address.

requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a packet protected with Handshake keys.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the receipt as confirmation that the peer successfully processed an Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a valid Handshake-key-protected packet and inspect whether Initial-packet processing by the peer is treated as confirmed.

evidence.quote:
receipt of a packet protected with
   Handshake keys confirms that the peer successfully processed an
   Initial packet.

requirements.condition: An endpoint has successfully processed a Handshake packet from its peer.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may transition the peer address to validated.
requirements.why_checkable: The address-validation state can be inspected after successful processing of a peer Handshake packet.

evidence.quote:
Once an endpoint has successfully processed a
   Handshake packet from the peer, it can consider the peer address to
   have been validated.

requirements.condition: The peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint, and that connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may consider the peer address validated.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary connection-ID provenance and entropy and inspect the resulting address-validation state.

evidence.quote:
an endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated if
   the peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint and the
   connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy.

requirements.condition: A client successfully processes a packet whose authenticity or server possession is established using the Destination Connection ID from the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow the client to validate the server address as part of processing that packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can correlate the first Initial Destination Connection ID with processed server packets and inspect server-address validation state.

evidence.quote:
For the client, the value of the Destination Connection ID field in
   its first Initial packet allows it to validate the server address as
   a part of successfully processing any packet.

requirements.condition: The server sends Initial packets in response to the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the server Initial packets with keys derived from the Destination Connection ID value in the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet protection keys can be derived from the recorded Destination Connection ID and used to verify the server Initial packets.

evidence.quote:
Initial packets from
   the server are protected with keys that are derived from this value

requirements.condition: The server sends a Version Negotiation or Retry packet as the alternative proof based on the client's first Initial Destination Connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Echo the value in a Version Negotiation packet, or include it in the Integrity Tag of a Retry packet, according to the packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: The fields and integrity input of Version Negotiation and Retry packets can be decoded and compared with the first Initial Destination Connection ID.

evidence.quote:
Alternatively, the value is echoed
   by the server in Version Negotiation packets (Section 6) or included
   in the Integrity Tag in Retry packets (Section 5.8 of [QUIC-TLS]).

requirements.condition: A server has not yet validated the client address.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit bytes sent to no more than three times the number of bytes received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending more than three times the number of bytes received before validating the client address.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can track received and transmitted byte totals before validation and verify the 3:1 bound.

evidence.quote:
Prior to validating the client address, servers MUST NOT send more
   than three times as many bytes as the number of bytes they have
   received.

requirements.condition: A server computes the received-byte allowance before address validation for datagrams uniquely attributable to one connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Count all payload bytes received in those datagrams.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting any received payload bytes from uniquely attributable datagrams when computing the anti-amplification allowance.
requirements.why_checkable: Datagram payload lengths and connection attribution can be recorded and compared with the server's anti-amplification accounting.

evidence.quote:
For the purposes of
   avoiding amplification prior to address validation, servers MUST
   count all of the payload bytes received in datagrams that are
   uniquely attributed to a single connection.

requirements.condition: A received datagram is uniquely attributed to one connection and its packets are successfully processed or all discarded.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the datagram's payload bytes in received-byte accounting in either case.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Excluding a uniquely attributable datagram merely because all of its packets were discarded.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can send both processable and wholly discarded packets in attributable datagrams and inspect the accounting total.

evidence.quote:
This includes datagrams
   that contain packets that are successfully processed and datagrams
   that contain packets that are all discarded.

requirements.condition: A client sends a UDP datagram containing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the UDP payload is at least 1200 bytes, adding PADDING frames when necessary to reach that size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending a UDP datagram containing an Initial packet with a UDP payload smaller than 1200 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted datagram's UDP payload length and any PADDING frames can be inspected directly.

evidence.quote:
Clients MUST ensure that UDP datagrams containing Initial packets
   have UDP payloads of at least 1200 bytes, adding PADDING frames as
   necessary.

requirements.condition: A client's Probe Timeout fires during connection establishment.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a packet on the Probe Timeout.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allowing the Probe Timeout to expire without sending a packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A controlled PTO event can be triggered and outbound packet emission observed.

evidence.quote:
To
   prevent this deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a Probe Timeout
   (PTO); see Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

requirements.condition: A client must send on a Probe Timeout and does not have Handshake keys.
requirements.required_behavior: Send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram containing at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending only a non-Initial packet or using a UDP datagram smaller than 1200 bytes in this PTO branch.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can fire a PTO before Handshake keys exist and inspect the packet type and datagram size.

evidence.quote:
the client
   MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram that contains at least
   1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys

requirements.condition: A client must send on a Probe Timeout and has Handshake keys.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a Handshake packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Failing to send a Handshake packet in this PTO branch.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can fire a PTO after Handshake keys become available and inspect the emitted packet type.

evidence.quote:
and otherwise send a
   Handshake packet.

requirements.condition: Client-address validation is performed before completion of the handshake using this token mechanism.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the address-validation token in the Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The Initial packet can be decoded to verify the presence and placement of the token used for pre-handshake validation.

evidence.quote:
QUIC uses a token in the Initial packet
   to provide address validation prior to completing the handshake.

requirements.condition: A client supplies a token for address validation in an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a token delivered either by a Retry packet during the current connection establishment or by a NEW_TOKEN frame in a previous connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Token provenance can be recorded and checked against prior Retry packets or NEW_TOKEN frames.

evidence.quote:
This token is delivered to the client during connection establishment
   with a Retry packet (see Section 8.1.2) or in a previous connection
   using the NEW_TOKEN frame (see Section 8.1.3).

requirements.condition: A server sends data, including before address validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep server transmissions within the limits set by the congestion controller in addition to applicable pre-validation sending limits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending beyond congestion-controller limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Server transmissions can be compared with the active congestion controller's current sending allowance.

evidence.quote:
servers are also constrained in what they can send by the limits set
   by the congestion controller.

requirements.condition: A client determines its sending limit under the constraints discussed in this passage.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the congestion controller's sending constraint.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Applying the server's pre-address-validation anti-amplification sending limit to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect whether client sending is governed by congestion control without imposing the server-only anti-amplification limit.

evidence.quote:
Clients are only constrained by the
   congestion controller.

requirements.condition: When constructing a token to be sent in a NEW_TOKEN frame or a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Construct the token so that the server can identify whether and how it was provided to the client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not construct the token in a form that prevents the server from identifying how it was provided to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can generate tokens through both delivery mechanisms and verify that the server can distinguish their provenance and apply mechanism-specific handling.

evidence.quote: A token sent in a NEW_TOKEN frame or a Retry packet MUST be constructed in a way that allows the server to identify how it was provided to a client.

requirements.condition: The client has received a Retry packet containing a token and subsequently sends an Initial packet for that connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The client includes the Retry token in every subsequent Initial packet for that connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not send a subsequent Initial packet for that connection without repeating the Retry token.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces or generated Initial packets can be inspected to verify that every Initial sent after receipt of Retry contains the supplied token.

evidence.quote: This token MUST be repeated by the client in all Initial packets it sends for that connection after it receives the Retry packet.

requirements.condition: A server processes an Initial packet containing a token previously provided in a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The server either refuses the connection or permits the connection to proceed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not choose a response outcome other than refusing the connection or permitting it to proceed.
requirements.why_checkable: The server's resulting connection state and emitted packets can be checked to ensure the outcome is one of the two permitted branches.

evidence.quote: In response to processing an Initial packet containing a token that was provided in a Retry packet, a server cannot send another Retry packet; it can only refuse the connection or permit it to proceed.

requirements.condition: A server processes an Initial packet containing a token previously provided in a Retry packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not send another Retry packet in response.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can provide a Retry token in a subsequent Initial and verify that the server does not emit a second Retry.

evidence.quote: In response to processing an Initial packet containing a token that was provided in a Retry packet, a server cannot send another Retry packet;

requirements.condition: A server receives an otherwise valid client Initial containing an invalid Retry token.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not rely on the client accepting another Retry token.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's invalid-token branch can be inspected or exercised to determine whether it attempts recovery by issuing and relying on another Retry token.

evidence.quote: If a server receives a client Initial that contains an invalid Retry token but is otherwise valid, it knows the client will not accept another Retry token.

requirements.condition: A server receives an otherwise valid client Initial containing an invalid Retry token.
requirements.required_behavior: The server should immediately close the connection.
requirements.error_behavior: The immediate close should use an INVALID_TOKEN error.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused test can send an otherwise valid Initial with an invalid Retry token and observe whether the server immediately closes with INVALID_TOKEN.

evidence.quote: Instead, the server SHOULD immediately close (Section 10.2) the connection with an INVALID_TOKEN error.

requirements.condition: The server closes in response to an otherwise valid client Initial containing an invalid Retry token, before connection state has been established.
requirements.required_behavior: The server does not enter the closing period.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not transition the connection into the closing-period state.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's state transition after rejecting the invalid Retry token can be inspected or tested to verify that no closing-period state or timer is entered.

evidence.quote: Note that a server has not established any state for the connection at this point and so does not enter the closing period.

requirements.condition: During a connection, when a server chooses to support address validation for later connections.
requirements.required_behavior: The server is permitted to provide the client with an address validation token usable on a subsequent connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Server output and the token's acceptance on a subsequent connection can be observed in protocol tests.

evidence.quote: A server MAY provide clients with an address validation token during one connection that can be used on a subsequent connection.

requirements.condition: A Retry replaces the token with a newer token during the connection attempt.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must use the newer Retry token for subsequent Initial packets instead of continuing to use the replaced token.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not continue placing the replaced token in subsequent Initial packets.
requirements.why_checkable: The exception explicitly establishes a token replacement transition that can be checked in packets sent after Retry.

evidence.quote: The client MUST include the token in all Initial packets it sends, unless a Retry replaces the token with a newer one.

requirements.condition: The client is using an address validation token on a future connection and no Retry has replaced it with a newer token.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must include that token in every Initial packet it sends.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not omit the token from any Initial packet while the token remains current.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet trace can verify token presence in every Initial packet and account for replacement by Retry.

evidence.quote: The client MUST include the token in all Initial packets it sends, unless a Retry replaces the token with a newer one.

requirements.condition: A client has received a token in a Retry packet and later starts a different connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not use the Retry token on the future connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can retain a Retry token, initiate a later connection, and inspect whether the client reuses it.

evidence.quote: The client MUST NOT use the token provided in a Retry for future connections.

requirements.condition: A server receives an Initial packet that does not carry the expected token.
requirements.required_behavior: The server is permitted to discard the Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The server's handling of a crafted Initial packet missing the expected token is directly observable.

evidence.quote: Servers MAY discard any Initial packet that does not carry the expected token.

requirements.condition: A server creates an address validation token that can be used after its issuance.
requirements.required_behavior: The token should carry or otherwise have an expiration time, represented either explicitly or through an issued timestamp from which expiration can be calculated.
requirements.why_checkable: Token generation and validation tests can determine whether expiration metadata exists and whether expiration can be calculated.

evidence.quote: Thus, a token SHOULD have an expiration time, which could be either an explicit expiration time or an issued timestamp that can be used to dynamically calculate the expiration time.

requirements.condition: A server issues a token using a NEW_TOKEN frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The token must not expose information that enables an observer to link its values to the connection on which it was issued.
requirements.why_checkable: The token's externally visible representation can be inspected across connections for exposed linkable values.

evidence.quote: A token issued with NEW_TOKEN MUST NOT include information that would allow values to be linked by an observer to the connection on which it was issued.

requirements.condition: A NEW_TOKEN token contains the previous connection ID or addressing information.
requirements.required_behavior: Such connection-specific values must be encrypted if they are included.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The token must not include the previous connection ID or addressing information in unencrypted form.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated tokens can be inspected to determine whether connection IDs or addressing information appear in plaintext.

evidence.quote: For example, it cannot include the previous connection ID or addressing information, unless the values are encrypted.

requirements.condition: A server sends NEW_TOKEN frames, excluding retransmissions or replacement sends that repair loss of a previously sent NEW_TOKEN frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The server must ensure that each sent NEW_TOKEN frame is unique across all clients.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not send the same NEW_TOKEN frame to different clients or in distinct non-loss-repair issuances.
requirements.why_checkable: NEW_TOKEN frames collected across clients and issuances can be compared for uniqueness while identifying loss-repair sends.

evidence.quote: A server MUST ensure that every NEW_TOKEN frame it sends is unique across all clients, with the exception of those sent to repair losses of previously sent NEW_TOKEN frames.

requirements.condition: A client receives a token in a NEW_TOKEN frame on a connection that is authoritative for one or more servers.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must treat the token as applicable to any server for which that connection is considered authoritative.
requirements.why_checkable: Client token-selection behavior can be tested against server identities covered by the issuing connection's authority.

evidence.quote: A token received in a NEW_TOKEN frame is applicable to any server that the connection is considered authoritative for (e.g., server names included in the certificate).

requirements.condition: The client connects to a server for which it retains a token that is both applicable and unused.
requirements.required_behavior: The client should place that token in the Token field of its Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can preload an applicable unused token and inspect the Initial packet's Token field.

evidence.quote: When connecting to a server for which the client retains an applicable and unused token, it SHOULD include that token in the Token field of its Initial packet.

requirements.condition: The client knows that the token-issuing server and the destination server jointly manage tokens.
requirements.required_behavior: The client is permitted to include a token that would otherwise not be applicable to the destination server.
requirements.why_checkable: The stated exception can be exercised by configuring known joint token management and observing token inclusion.

evidence.quote: A client MUST NOT include a token that is not applicable to the server that it is connecting to, unless the client has the knowledge that the server that issued the token and the server the client is connecting to are jointly managing the tokens.

requirements.condition: The client connects to a server to which a retained token is not applicable, and the client does not know that the issuing and destination servers jointly manage tokens.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not include the inapplicable token in the connection's Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Token selection can be tested with an inapplicable token and without joint-management knowledge.

evidence.quote: A client MUST NOT include a token that is not applicable to the server that it is connecting to, unless the client has the knowledge that the server that issued the token and the server the client is connecting to are jointly managing the tokens.

requirements.condition: The client has a token from a previous connection to the same server.
requirements.required_behavior: The client is permitted to use that token for the new connection, subject to the other token-use constraints.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can retain a token from an earlier connection to the server and verify that the implementation accepts it for selection.

evidence.quote: A client MAY use a token from any previous connection to that server.

requirements.condition: A client has retained a token obtained from a Retry packet and initiates a subsequent connection attempt.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not use the Retry token in the subsequent connection attempt.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can complete or abandon the original attempt, begin another, and check that the old Retry token is not reused.

evidence.quote: In comparison, a token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt and cannot be used in subsequent connection attempts.

requirements.condition: A client obtains a token in a Retry packet during a connection attempt.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must use the token immediately during that same connection attempt.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets following Retry can be inspected to verify immediate use within the active attempt.

evidence.quote: In comparison, a token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt and cannot be used in subsequent connection attempts.

requirements.condition: A client has already used a token obtained from a NEW_TOKEN frame in one connection attempt.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client should not reuse that token for a different connection attempt.
requirements.why_checkable: Token values sent across separate connection attempts can be compared to detect reuse.

evidence.quote: A client SHOULD NOT reuse a token from a NEW_TOKEN frame for different connection attempts.

requirements.condition: A server receives an Initial packet containing an address validation token and has not already completed address validation.
requirements.required_behavior: The server must attempt to validate the token.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not skip token validation while the client address remains unvalidated.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation or crafted valid and invalid tokens can demonstrate whether validation is attempted before address validation completes.

evidence.quote: When a server receives an Initial packet with an address validation token, it MUST attempt to validate the token, unless it has already completed address validation.

requirements.condition: The server has already completed address validation when it receives an Initial packet containing a token.
requirements.required_behavior: The server is permitted to omit another token-validation attempt.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can first complete address validation and then determine whether a later token triggers redundant validation.

evidence.quote: When a server receives an Initial packet with an address validation token, it MUST attempt to validate the token, unless it has already completed address validation.

requirements.condition: Validation of an address validation token fails because the token is invalid.
requirements.required_behavior: The server should continue processing with the client address treated as unvalidated and may send a Retry packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server should not treat the client address as validated based on the invalid token.
requirements.error_behavior: Handle the invalid token by proceeding as though the client did not have a validated address rather than granting validation.
requirements.why_checkable: An invalid token can be injected and the resulting validation state and possible Retry response observed.

evidence.quote: If the token is invalid, then the server SHOULD proceed as if the client did not have a validated address, including potentially sending a Retry packet.

requirements.condition: Validation of the address validation token succeeds.
requirements.required_behavior: The server should allow the handshake to proceed.
requirements.why_checkable: A valid token can be supplied and subsequent handshake progress observed.

evidence.quote: If the validation succeeds, the server SHOULD then allow the handshake to proceed.

requirements.condition: A server uses tokens to carry information for later client-address validation.
requirements.required_behavior: The server can restrict token-carried information to information needed for client-address validation.
requirements.why_checkable: Token contents can be inspected at the point before encryption to determine whether they contain information unrelated to address validation, but the permissive wording and undefined scope of "needed" do not establish a definite implementation requirement.

evidence.quote: To avoid attacks that exploit this property, a server can limit its use of tokens to only the information needed to validate client addresses.

requirements.condition: A server uses address validation tokens that are not authenticated by the cryptographic handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage suggests limiting token-carried information but uses permissive language and does not establish a definite implementation obligation.

evidence.quote: To avoid attacks that exploit this property, a server can limit its use of tokens to only the information needed to validate client addresses.

requirements.condition: A client has obtained a token on one connection and attempts another connection using the same version.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation permits the client to use the token for the connection attempt.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not categorically reject token reuse solely because the token was obtained on another connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can obtain a token on one connection and verify that the client permits its use on another connection attempt using the same version.

evidence.quote: Clients MAY use tokens obtained on one connection for any connection attempt using the same version.

requirements.condition: A client selects a token for a connection attempt using the same version.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation permits token selection without matching application protocols, session tickets, or other connection properties.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not require those other connection properties to match as a prerequisite for selecting the token.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary application protocols, session tickets, and other connection properties while holding the version constant and verify that token selection remains permitted.

evidence.quote: When selecting a token to use, clients do not need to consider other properties of the connection that is being attempted, including the choice of possible application protocols, session tickets, or other connection properties.

requirements.condition: When generating an address validation token
requirements.required_behavior: The token must be difficult to guess.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not generate readily guessable address validation tokens.
requirements.why_checkable: Token-generation entropy, unpredictability, or resistance to practical guessing can be assessed from the implementation and focused tests.

evidence.quote: An address validation token MUST be difficult to guess.

requirements.condition: When the server uses a remembered random value as the means of making an address validation token difficult to guess
requirements.required_behavior: A random value with at least 128 bits of entropy is sufficient if the server remembers the value sent to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: The random-value entropy and whether the server retains the issued value are observable implementation properties, and the passage directly identifies their combination as sufficient.

evidence.quote: Including a random value with at least 128 bits of entropy in the token would be sufficient, but this depends on the server remembering the value it sends to clients.

requirements.condition: When a token-based scheme offloads address-validation state to the client
requirements.required_behavior: The token must be integrity-protected against client modification and falsification.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not rely on an unprotected client-held token for this design.
requirements.why_checkable: The token construction and validation paths can be inspected and tested for cryptographic integrity protection.

evidence.quote: For this design to work, the token MUST be covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients.

requirements.condition: When a client presents a modified, fabricated, or guessed token value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not accept the token merely as a syntactically valid value without successful integrity verification.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat tokens that fail integrity verification as unacceptable.
requirements.why_checkable: This rejection behavior follows directly from the required integrity protection and can be tested with modified or fabricated tokens.

evidence.quote: Without integrity protection, malicious clients could generate or guess values for tokens that would be accepted by the server.

requirements.condition: When assigning access to the token integrity-protection key
requirements.why_checkable: Key access can be inspected, but the sentence states who requires access rather than clearly prohibiting access by any other component or party.

evidence.quote: Only the server requires access to the integrity protection key for tokens.

requirements.condition: When the server sends a token in a Retry packet
requirements.required_behavior: The token should include information that allows verification that the source port in subsequent client packets remains constant.
requirements.why_checkable: The Retry-token contents and validation logic can be inspected and exercised using a changed source port.

evidence.quote: Tokens sent in Retry packets SHOULD include information that allows the server to verify that the source IP address and port in client packets remain constant.

requirements.condition: When the server sends a token in a Retry packet
requirements.required_behavior: The token should include information that allows verification that the source IP address in subsequent client packets remains constant.
requirements.why_checkable: The Retry-token contents and validation logic can be inspected and exercised using a changed source IP address.

evidence.quote: Tokens sent in Retry packets SHOULD include information that allows the server to verify that the source IP address and port in client packets remain constant.

requirements.condition: When the server sends a token in a NEW_TOKEN frame
requirements.required_behavior: The token must include information that allows the server to verify whether the client IP address has changed since token issuance.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not issue a NEW_TOKEN token lacking information sufficient for that verification.
requirements.why_checkable: The token construction and later validation behavior can be tested by presenting the token from the original and a changed client IP address.

evidence.quote: Tokens sent in NEW_TOKEN frames MUST include information that allows the server to verify that the client IP address has not changed from when the token was issued.

requirements.condition: When deciding whether to send a Retry packet using a token from a NEW_TOKEN frame, including after a client-address change
requirements.why_checkable: The decision path is observable, but the sentence only describes an available option and imposes no required or forbidden implementation behavior.

evidence.quote: Servers can use tokens from NEW_TOKEN frames in deciding not to send a Retry packet, even if the client address has changed.

requirements.condition: If the client IP address has changed
requirements.required_behavior: The server must adhere to the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not exceed the anti-amplification limit because it received or used a token.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can change the client IP address and measure whether the server's transmitted data remains within its implemented anti-amplification limit.

evidence.quote: If the client IP address has changed, the server MUST adhere to the anti-amplification limit; see Section 8.

requirements.condition: When processing address validation tokens that an attacker could replay
requirements.required_behavior: The server must implement controls that prevent token replay or limit its effectiveness or extent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not permit unrestricted replay of tokens.
requirements.why_checkable: Replay controls such as one-time use, replay tracking, or bounded validity can be identified and tested by repeatedly presenting the same token.

evidence.quote: To protect against such attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited.

requirements.condition: When accepting a token that was sent in a Retry packet
requirements.required_behavior: The server should restrict acceptance of the token to a short validity period.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server should not continue accepting a Retry token beyond its short validity period.
requirements.error_behavior: Reject an expired Retry token.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's Retry-token lifetime and its response to an expired token can be inspected and tested, though the precise duration is implementation-defined.

evidence.quote: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time, as they are returned immediately by clients.

requirements.condition: When processing a token provided in a NEW_TOKEN frame
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server should not accept the same NEW_TOKEN token multiple times.
requirements.error_behavior: Reject a repeated use of a NEW_TOKEN token.
requirements.why_checkable: Repeated presentation of the same NEW_TOKEN token can directly test whether more than one use is accepted.

evidence.quote: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames (Section 19.7) need to be valid for longer but SHOULD NOT be accepted multiple times.

requirements.condition: When setting the validity period of a token provided in a NEW_TOKEN frame
requirements.required_behavior: The token is described as needing a longer validity period than a Retry token.
requirements.why_checkable: Token lifetimes can be compared, but the passage does not define how much longer they must remain valid or express an unambiguous normative constraint.

evidence.quote: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames (Section 19.7) need to be valid for longer

requirements.condition: When the server can feasibly enforce single-use tokens
requirements.required_behavior: The server is encouraged to permit each token to be used only once.
requirements.why_checkable: Single-use enforcement can be tested by replaying a consumed token, but “encouraged” and “if possible” do not establish an unambiguous implementation requirement.

evidence.quote: Servers are encouraged to allow tokens to be used only once, if possible

requirements.condition: When constructing an address validation token
requirements.why_checkable: Client-specific information in a token can be inspected, but this permission does not require its presence or impose a definite acceptance behavior.

evidence.quote: tokens MAY include additional information about clients to further narrow applicability or reuse.

requirements.condition: When validating reachability in the return direction of a path.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use acknowledgments as proof of return-path reachability.
requirements.why_checkable: A test or code inspection can verify that receipt of acknowledgments does not cause the return path to be marked validated.

evidence.quote:
Path validation does not validate that a peer can send in the return
   direction.  Acknowledgments cannot be used for return path validation
   because they contain insufficient entropy and might be spoofed.

requirements.condition: When determining whether each direction of a path is reachable.
requirements.required_behavior: Determine reachability independently for each direction; allow return reachability to be established only by the peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not infer return reachability solely from locally established forward reachability.
requirements.why_checkable: Directional path-validation state transitions can be inspected or tested to ensure validation in one direction does not automatically validate the reverse direction.

evidence.quote:
Endpoints independently determine reachability on each direction of a
   path, and therefore return reachability can only be established by
   the peer.

requirements.condition: When constructing a packet containing a PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE frame used for path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit other frames to be included in the same packet, including PADDING with PATH_CHALLENGE.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject or treat the packet as invalid merely because other frames accompany PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet construction and parsing tests can verify that these path-validation frames may be coalesced with other frames.

evidence.quote:
An endpoint MAY include other frames with the PATH_CHALLENGE and
   PATH_RESPONSE frames used for path validation.  In particular, an
   endpoint can include PADDING frames with a PATH_CHALLENGE frame for
   Path Maximum Transmission Unit Discovery (PMTUD); see Section 14.2.1.

requirements.condition: When sending a PATH_RESPONSE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the endpoint to include its own PATH_CHALLENGE frame in the same packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject this frame combination merely because PATH_CHALLENGE accompanies PATH_RESPONSE.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet parser or generator can be tested with PATH_CHALLENGE and PATH_RESPONSE present together.

evidence.quote:
An endpoint can also include its own PATH_CHALLENGE frame when
   sending a PATH_RESPONSE frame.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends a path probe from a new local address.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a new connection ID for the probe.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse a connection ID previously used from another local address for that probe.
requirements.why_checkable: Probe generation can be tested or inspected to correlate each newly used local address with a new connection ID.

evidence.quote:
An endpoint uses a new connection ID for probes sent from a new local
   address; see Section 9.5.  When probing a new path, an endpoint can
   ensure that its peer has an unused connection ID available for
   responses.

requirements.condition: When probing a new path and the peer's active_connection_id_limit permits issuance of another connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may send NEW_CONNECTION_ID and PATH_CHALLENGE in the same packet so that the peer has an unused connection ID for its response.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-generation tests can verify conditional coalescing of NEW_CONNECTION_ID with PATH_CHALLENGE and the resulting availability of an unused connection ID.

evidence.quote:
responses.  Sending NEW_CONNECTION_ID and PATH_CHALLENGE frames in
   the same packet, if the peer's active_connection_id_limit permits,
   ensures that an unused connection ID will be available to the peer
   when sending a response.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint simultaneously probes multiple paths using new local addresses.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the number of simultaneously probed paths at or below the number of extra connection IDs previously supplied by the peer, and use a previously unused connection ID for each new local address.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not simultaneously probe more new-local-address paths than the available extra connection IDs, and do not reuse a connection ID for a new local address.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime tests can vary the number of supplied extra connection IDs and verify both the probe-count bound and unique unused connection-ID assignment.

evidence.quote:
An endpoint can choose to simultaneously probe multiple paths.  The
   number of simultaneous paths used for probes is limited by the number
   of extra connection IDs its peer has previously supplied, since each
   new local address used for a probe requires a previously unused
   connection ID.

requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PATH_CHALLENGE frame containing an unpredictable payload on the path being validated.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can initiate path validation and inspect the selected path and the emitted frame type and payload.

evidence.quote: To initiate path validation, an endpoint sends a PATH_CHALLENGE frame containing an unpredictable payload on the path to be validated.

requirements.condition: When guarding path validation against packet loss.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to be sent.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that the implementation permits transmission of multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames during path validation.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MAY send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to guard against packet loss.

requirements.condition: When constructing a packet containing PATH_CHALLENGE frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in one packet unless a justified exception to the SHOULD NOT applies.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet inspection can count the PATH_CHALLENGE frames contained in each packet.

evidence.quote: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.

requirements.condition: When probing a new path using packets that contain PATH_CHALLENGE frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the probing frequency to no more than the endpoint's Initial-packet sending frequency unless a justified exception to the SHOULD NOT applies.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send such path probes more frequently than Initial packets would be sent unless a justified exception applies.
requirements.why_checkable: A timing test can compare the implementation's PATH_CHALLENGE probe rate with its Initial-packet transmission rate.

evidence.quote: An endpoint SHOULD NOT probe a new path with packets containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame more frequently than it would send an Initial packet.

requirements.condition: Whenever an endpoint constructs a PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame, enabling the corresponding peer response to be associated with that challenge.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use predictable challenge data or omit unpredictable data from any PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated PATH_CHALLENGE payloads can be inspected for use of the implementation's unpredictable-data mechanism and response-to-challenge association.

evidence.quote: The endpoint MUST use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame so that it can associate the peer's response with the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE.

requirements.condition: When sending a datagram containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame and the path's anti-amplification limit permits a 1200-byte datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: Expand the datagram to at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the PATH_CHALLENGE datagram below 1200 bytes when the anti-amplification limit permits that size.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can measure each qualifying PATH_CHALLENGE datagram and evaluate the anti-amplification allowance for its path.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_CHALLENGE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, unless the anti-amplification limit for the path does not permit sending a datagram of this size.

requirements.condition: When the anti-amplification limit prevents an endpoint from expanding a PATH_CHALLENGE datagram to 1200 bytes.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the path MTU in an unvalidated state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat the path MTU as validated based on that undersized datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-based test can force the anti-amplification exception and verify that path-MTU validation is not recorded.

evidence.quote: When an endpoint is unable to expand the datagram size to 1200 bytes due to the anti-amplification limit, the path MTU will not be validated.

requirements.condition: After an initial path validation used a PATH_CHALLENGE datagram smaller than 1200 bytes because of the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not consider the required path-MTU validation complete without the second validation using a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger the undersized anti-amplification case and verify a subsequent validation attempt and its datagram size.

evidence.quote: To ensure that the path MTU is large enough, the endpoint MUST perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.

requirements.condition: When a datagram appears too small but contains a PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Retain the datagram for normal handling despite its apparent small size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard the datagram merely because it appears too small.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver apparently undersized datagrams containing either frame type and observe whether the implementation discards them for size alone.

evidence.quote: Unlike other cases where datagrams are expanded, endpoints MUST NOT discard datagrams that appear to be too small when they contain PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE.

requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PATH_RESPONSE frame containing an exact echo of the data from the received PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a PATH_CHALLENGE frame and verify that the endpoint sends a PATH_RESPONSE whose data matches the challenge data exactly.

evidence.quote: On receiving a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, an endpoint MUST respond by echoing the data contained in the PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a PATH_RESPONSE frame.

requirements.condition: An endpoint has a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame ready for transmission and congestion control does not constrain transmission.
requirements.required_behavior: Transmit the packet without delay.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Delay transmission of the packet for a reason other than congestion control.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can determine whether a ready PATH_RESPONSE packet is delayed and whether congestion control was constraining transmission at that time.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT delay transmission of a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless constrained by congestion control.

requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a PATH_RESPONSE for a received PATH_CHALLENGE.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the PATH_RESPONSE on the same network path on which the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE was received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the PATH_RESPONSE on a different network path.
requirements.why_checkable: A multipath test can identify the ingress path of a PATH_CHALLENGE and compare it with the egress path of the corresponding PATH_RESPONSE.

evidence.quote: A PATH_RESPONSE frame MUST be sent on the network path where the PATH_CHALLENGE frame was received.

requirements.condition: An endpoint initiated path validation and evaluates the received PATH_RESPONSE.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Require the PATH_RESPONSE to have arrived on the same network path on which the PATH_CHALLENGE was sent as a condition of accepting the validation response.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can initiate validation, return the matching PATH_RESPONSE through a different observable path, and verify that the initiator does not enforce same-path receipt.

evidence.quote: This requirement MUST NOT be enforced by the endpoint that initiates path validation, as that would enable an attack on migration; see Section 9.3.3.

requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a datagram containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame, and expansion to 1200 bytes would not cause the datagram to exceed the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Expand the datagram to a size of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the datagram at a size below 1200 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The general 1200-byte expansion rule and its adjacent anti-amplification exception can be combined and checked by observing the datagram size and current amplification allowance.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_RESPONSE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.

requirements.condition: Expanding a datagram containing a PATH_RESPONSE would cause the resulting data to exceed the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Send without performing the otherwise required expansion.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Expand the datagram beyond the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish a known anti-amplification allowance and verify that padding or other expansion is not applied when it would exceed that allowance.

evidence.quote: However, an endpoint MUST NOT expand the datagram containing the PATH_RESPONSE if the resulting data exceeds the anti-amplification limit.

requirements.condition: An endpoint is responding to a single PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame attributable to that PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver one PATH_CHALLENGE and count the PATH_RESPONSE frames generated in response, requiring the count not to exceed one.

evidence.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame in response to one PATH_CHALLENGE frame; see Section 13.3.

requirements.condition: A PATH_RESPONSE frame is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Declare path validation successful only when the PATH_RESPONSE contains the data sent in a previous PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not declare path validation successful based on a PATH_RESPONSE whose data does not match data sent in a previous PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can send matching and nonmatching PATH_RESPONSE data and observe whether path validation transitions to successful.

evidence.quote: Path validation succeeds when a PATH_RESPONSE frame is received that contains the data that was sent in a previous PATH_CHALLENGE frame.

requirements.condition: A valid PATH_RESPONSE is received on any network path.
requirements.required_behavior: Mark the network path on which the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE was sent as validated, regardless of the path on which the PATH_RESPONSE arrived.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat the PATH_RESPONSE arrival path as the validated path merely because the response arrived on it.
requirements.why_checkable: A multi-path test can deliver the response on a path different from the challenge path and inspect which path the implementation validates.

evidence.quote: A PATH_RESPONSE frame received on any network path validates the path on which the PATH_CHALLENGE was sent.

requirements.condition: A PATH_CHALLENGE is sent in a datagram smaller than 1200 bytes, and its response validates the peer address.
requirements.required_behavior: Mark the path as validated while leaving the path MTU unvalidated.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat the path MTU as validated by this exchange.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can complete validation using a sub-1200-byte challenge datagram and separately inspect path-validation and MTU-validation state.

evidence.quote: If an endpoint sends a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram that is not expanded to at least 1200 bytes and if the response to it validates the peer address, the path is validated but not the path MTU.

requirements.condition: The peer address was validated using a PATH_CHALLENGE datagram that was not expanded to at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.required_behavior: Initiate another path validation using a datagram expanded to at least 1200 bytes to verify support for the required path MTU.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the additional expanded-datagram path validation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can validate an address with an undersized challenge datagram and observe whether the endpoint subsequently initiates validation with a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.

evidence.quote: However, the endpoint MUST initiate another path validation with an expanded datagram to verify that the path supports the required MTU.

requirements.condition: An acknowledgment is received for a packet containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not mark the path as validated solely because that packet was acknowledged.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can acknowledge a packet carrying PATH_CHALLENGE without returning the corresponding PATH_RESPONSE and verify that the path remains unvalidated.

evidence.quote: Receipt of an acknowledgment for a packet containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame is not adequate validation, since the acknowledgment can be spoofed by a malicious peer.

requirements.condition: An endpoint is attempting to validate a path.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat path validation as failed only when the endpoint abandons its validation attempt.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat path validation as failed before the validation attempt is abandoned.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's validation state transitions can be observed to verify that failure occurs only following abandonment.

evidence.quote: Path validation only fails when the endpoint attempting to validate the path abandons its attempt to validate the path.

requirements.condition: An endpoint is performing path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a timer as the basis for abandoning path validation.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be inspected or tested to determine whether expiration of a timer controls abandonment.

evidence.quote: Endpoints SHOULD abandon path validation based on a timer.

requirements.condition: An endpoint sets the timer used to abandon path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the timer to three times the larger of the current PTO and the PTO for the new path, calculating the new-path PTO using kInitialRtt.
requirements.why_checkable: The configured timeout can be compared with the two PTO values and the specified multiplier.

evidence.quote: A value of three times the larger of the current PTO or the PTO for the new path (using kInitialRtt, as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY]) is RECOMMENDED.

requirements.condition: A single PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE frame is lost during timed path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow multiple PTOs to expire before failing path validation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not fail path validation solely because one PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE frame is lost.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-injection test can drop one validation frame and verify that validation is not immediately failed and that multiple PTO opportunities remain.

evidence.quote: This timeout allows for multiple PTOs to expire prior to failing path validation, so that loss of a single PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE frame does not cause path validation failure.

requirements.condition: An endpoint determines whether validation of a new path has succeeded.
requirements.required_behavior: Require receipt of a PATH_RESPONSE frame containing appropriate data before declaring path validation successful.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not declare path validation successful merely because packets containing other frames were received on the new path.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can send packets with non-PATH_RESPONSE frames or an inappropriate PATH_RESPONSE and verify that neither causes validation success.

evidence.quote: a PATH_RESPONSE frame with appropriate data is required for path validation to succeed.

requirements.condition: An endpoint abandons path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Mark or otherwise determine the path to be unusable.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue treating the abandoned path as usable.
requirements.why_checkable: The path state and subsequent path-selection behavior can be checked after abandonment.

evidence.quote: When an endpoint abandons path validation, it determines that the path is unusable.

requirements.condition: No paths are available.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may either wait for a new path to become available or close the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's behavior when all paths are unavailable can be observed and matched to either permitted outcome.

evidence.quote: If no paths are available, an endpoint can wait for a new path to become available or close the connection.

requirements.condition: The endpoint has no valid network path to its peer, while a network path exists but does not support the required MTU.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use NO_VIABLE_PATH to report this condition unless a network path exists but fails to support the required MTU.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint may signal the condition using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can vary path existence and MTU support and observe whether NO_VIABLE_PATH is emitted only in the stated circumstance.

evidence.quote: An endpoint that has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error, noting that this is only possible if the network path exists but does not support the required MTU (Section 14).

requirements.condition: Migration to a new path begins while validation of the old path is in progress.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage describes a common reason for abandonment but does not unambiguously require the implementation to abandon old-path validation in this situation.

evidence.quote: Primarily, this happens if a connection migration to a new path is initiated while a path validation on the old path is in progress.

requirements.condition: Before the handshake is confirmed as defined in Section 4.1.2 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not initiate connection migration.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can attempt migration before handshake confirmation and verify that the endpoint does not initiate it.

evidence.quote:
The design of QUIC relies on endpoints retaining a stable address for
   the duration of the handshake.  An endpoint MUST NOT initiate
   connection migration before the handshake is confirmed, as defined in

requirements.condition: When applying the connection ID reuse requirements in this section.

evidence.quote: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD begin sending all future packets to the new server address using the new connection ID and discontinue use of the old server address.

evidence.quote:
Initial packets use an AEAD function, the keys for which are derived
   using a value that is visible on the wire.  Initial packets therefore
   do not have effective confidentiality protection.  Initial protection
   exists to ensure that the sender of the packet is on the network
   path.  Any entity that receives an Initial packet from a client can
   recover the keys that will allow them to both read the contents of
   the packet and generate Initial packets that will be successfully
   authenticated at either endpoint.  The AEAD also protects Initial
   packets against accidental modification.

   a Stateless Reset (Section 10.3) in response to further packets that
   it receives.

evidence.quote:
A client MUST NOT reset the packet number for any packet number space
   after processing a Retry packet.  In particular, 0-RTT packets
   contain confidential information that will most likely be
   retransmitted on receiving a Retry packet.  The keys used to protect
   these new 0-RTT packets will not change as a result of responding to
   a Retry packet.  However, the data sent in these packets could be
   different than what was sent earlier.  Sending these new packets with
   the same packet number is likely to compromise the packet protection
   for those packets because the same key and nonce could be used to
   protect different content.  A server MAY abort the connection if it
   detects that the client reset the packet number.

requirements.condition: While a path is in the ECN testing period.
requirements.required_behavior: Bound the testing period by either a number of packets or a time limit selected by the endpoint, while sending enough marked packets to make received ECN counts informative.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's testing termination criterion and transmission of marked packets can be observed, though the exact sufficient packet quantity is not defined in this passage.

evidence.quote:
The testing period runs for a number of packets or a limited time, as
   determined by the endpoint.  The goal is not to limit the duration of
   the testing period but to ensure that enough marked packets are sent
   for received ECN counts to provide a clear indication of how the path
   treats marked packets.  Section 13.4.2 suggests limiting this to ten
   packets or three times the PTO.

requirements.condition: When selecting a suggested limit for the ECN testing period.
requirements.required_behavior: The testing period may be limited to ten packets or three times the PTO.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-count and elapsed-time limits are measurable, but this passage only offers a nonbinding suggestion and does not unambiguously constrain implementations.

requirements.condition: When a path is in the "unknown" ECN state, ECN counts in an ACK frame validate successfully, but no marked packet has been acknowledged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transition the path's ECN state to "capable" on the basis of that validation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can validate an ACK without any acknowledged marked packet and verify that the path does not enter the "capable" state.

evidence.quote:
After the testing period ends, the ECN state for the path becomes
   "unknown".  From the "unknown" state, successful validation of the
   ECN counts in an ACK frame (see Section 13.4.2.1) causes the ECN
   state for the path to become "capable", unless no marked packet has
   been acknowledged.

requirements.condition: When the ECN testing period for a path ends.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the path's ECN state to "unknown".
requirements.why_checkable: A test can end the testing period and inspect the path's resulting ECN state.

requirements.condition: When a path is in the "unknown" ECN state, ECN counts in an ACK frame validate successfully, and at least one marked packet has been acknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the path's ECN state to "capable".
requirements.why_checkable: A test can supply a successfully validated ACK with an acknowledged marked packet and inspect the state transition.

requirements.condition: When all marked packets on a path are ECN-CE marked.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to set the path's ECN state to "failed".
requirements.why_checkable: A test can arrange for every marked packet to be ECN-CE marked and observe whether the implementation exercises the explicitly permitted failure transition; the transition is optional.

evidence.quote:
If validation of ECN counts fails at any time, the ECN state for the
   affected path becomes "failed".  An endpoint can also mark the ECN
   state for a path as "failed" if marked packets are all declared lost
   or if they are all ECN-CE marked.

requirements.condition: When all marked packets on a path are declared lost.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to set the path's ECN state to "failed".
requirements.why_checkable: A test can declare every marked packet lost and observe whether the implementation exercises the explicitly permitted failure transition; the transition is optional.

requirements.condition: Whenever validation of ECN counts fails for a path.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the affected path's ECN state to "failed".
requirements.error_behavior: Treat failed ECN-count validation as failure of ECN capability for the affected path.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can induce ECN-count validation failure and inspect the affected path's ECN state.

evidence.quote:
If validation of ECN counts fails at any time, the ECN state for the

requirements.condition: When a path incorrectly modifies ECN markings.
requirements.required_behavior: Disable ECN for that path.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat incorrect modification of ECN markings as a reason to disable ECN.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can simulate inconsistent marking changes and verify that ECN is disabled for the path.

evidence.quote:
Following this algorithm ensures that ECN is rarely disabled for
   paths that properly support ECN.  Any path that incorrectly modifies
   markings will cause ECN to be disabled.  For those rare cases where
   marked packets are discarded by the path, the short duration of the
   testing period limits the number of losses incurred.
